title: Navigation, objects and a learning request
goal: Read an interface as a view of a domain model and verify meaning instead of guessing from window appearance.
outcomes: Distinguish a list, catalog item, document and report.
Trace a request from a row to related records.
Check filters and totals against synthetic inputs.
sections: Sections, commands and forms differ between applications. A universal instruction such as “press the third button on the left” ages quickly. Identify the purpose: a request list shows records, a request form shows one object, a report processes selected data. An empty list can indicate no records, a filter or restricted access. Test these hypotheses separately.

A1 provides a Nexus model with three requests. It supports learning to read rows and totals on a phone without an installed platform. The model is explicitly labeled and is not a 1C window. An actual empty infobase contains none of these documents; do not search for menus its configuration has not defined.

Catalogs commonly hold relatively stable domain objects such as customers and services. Documents commonly represent events or operations over time. This is a useful starting point, while exact behavior remains configuration-specific. “Alpha” is a customer presentation; the relation should preserve object identity, not merely a copied name string. Two customers can share a presentation.

REQ-001 and REQ-003 refer to one invented customer. Renaming that customer should not create a second identity. Repeatedly typing names instead of retaining references causes inconsistent spelling and grouping. A2 examines items and references in the official environment; here, learn to recognize the relationship in a data set.

Search helps locate a record; a filter specifies membership conditions. Conditions can combine, so record every active restriction before diagnosing a result. Status = New selects only REQ-001. Customer = Alpha selects REQ-001 and REQ-003. Durations total 105 minutes for all requests and 60 for Alpha. These are arithmetic control values, not measured service productivity.

A zero-valued row and no row are different observations. A report omitting closed requests does not prove deletion. Remove filters, locate the source document and inspect report settings first. Sorting changes presentation order; it does not by itself change the sum of selected values.

Start with known input data and a goal, such as finding Alpha’s requests and explaining their states. Verify identifiers as well as row count: two wrong records still produce a count of two. Then inspect an empty selection to distinguish no results from a loading error.

Model controls select statuses and show request details. This trains navigation without persisting 1C data. Candidate notes are separate per course; moving to P does not automatically award A1 completion. Identify the observation source in your protocol: Nexus model or official platform.

walkthrough.action: Select customer Alpha in the model.

walkthrough.expected: Three requests again; total remains 105 minutes.

exercises.task: For each request, identify its record, customer relation and status value.
exercises.criteria: Do not confuse presentation text with customer identity.

exercises.task: Design a check finding different records with the same name.
exercises.criteria: Use identity/code in addition to presentation.

lab.title: Observe navigation without confusing environments
lab.environment: Nexus provides the model; official A1 infobase supplies mode/About observations. Keep both parts of the protocol separate.
steps: Select each model status and record exact IDs and minute totals.
Open REQ-002 and identify values versus relations.
Record the official application name; if empty, explicitly state that no applied documents exist.
Compare the observations and explain why Nexus does not prove the documents exist in 1C.
expected: Clear separation of model and actual infobase.
lab.negative: Do not add arbitrary objects to an empty infobase to imitate the model without instructions.

mistakes: Check IDs and values, then count.

quiz.question: Customer = Alpha selects…
quiz.explanation: Alpha is related to the first and third model requests.

quiz.question: Ordinary sorting changes…
quiz.explanation: Presentation order does not change source values.

quiz.question: Documents shown in the Nexus model prove…
options: They already exist in your 1C infobase
quiz.explanation: 1C data requires a separate real observation.

review: Recall the control totals without hints.
